anchor.surface_text:
FOR THESE REASONS, THE COURT

1.  Declares the application admissible unanimously;

holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court found no preliminary objections and that the complaint was not manifestly ill-founded or inadmissible, thus declaring admissible.

holdings.text: Holds unanimously that there has been a violation of Article 11 of the Convention

anchor.surface_text: 2.  Holds unanimously that there has been a violation of Article 11 of the Convention;

holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court found interference with freedom of peaceful assembly due to disproportionate police intervention not justified or necessary in a democratic society.

holdings.text: Holds unanimously that there is no need to examine separately the applicants’ complaints under Articles 13 and 14 of the Convention

anchor.surface_text: 3.  Holds unanimously that there is no need to examine separately the applicants’ complaints under Articles 13 and 14 of the Convention;

holdings.reasoning_summary: Given the finding of violation of Article 11, the Court considered it unnecessary to separately examine complaints under Articles 13 and 14.

holdings.text: Holds by 5 votes to 2 that the finding of a violation of Article 11 in itself constitutes sufficient just satisfaction for the non-pecuniary damage sustained by the applicants

anchor.surface_text: 4.  Holds by 5 votes to 2 that the finding of a violation of Article 11 in itself constitutes sufficient just satisfaction for the non-pecuniary damage sustained by the applicants;

holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court decided that the violation finding sufficed as compensation for non-pecuniary damage, rejecting separate damages claim.

holdings.text: Holds unanimously that the respondent State is to pay the applicants, within three months from the date on which the judgment becomes final in accordance with Article 44 § 2 of the Convention, a total of EUR 1,000 (one thousand euros), plus any tax that may be chargeable to the applicants, in respect of costs and expenses

anchor.surface_text:
5.  Holds unanimously

(a)  that the respondent State is to pay the applicants, within three months from the date on which the judgment becomes final in accordance with Article 44 § 2 of the Convention, a total of EUR 1,000 (one thousand euros), plus any tax that may be chargeable to the applicants, in respect of costs and expenses, to be converted into the currency of the respondent State at the rate applicable at the date of settlement;

holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court awarded costs and expenses to the applicants in the amount of EUR 1,000, considering the claims reasonable and necessary.

holdings.text: Holds unanimously that from the expiry of the above-mentioned three months until settlement simple interest shall be payable on the above amount at a rate equal to the marginal lending rate of the European Central Bank during the default period plus three percentage points

anchor.surface_text: (b)  that from the expiry of the above-mentioned three months until settlement simple interest shall be payable on the above amount at a rate equal to the marginal lending rate of the European Central Bank during the default period plus three percentage points;

holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court ordered default interest on the costs awarded, calculated at ECB marginal lending rate plus three percentage points.

anchor.surface_text: The Court recalls that the Contracting States can impose limitations on holding a demonstration in a given place for public security reasons. Nevertheless, although a demonstration in a public place may cause some disruption to ordinary life, including disruption of traffic, it is important for the public authorities to show a certain degree of tolerance towards peaceful gatherings if the freedom of assembly guaranteed by Article 11 of the Convention is not to be deprived of its substance (see Galstyan v. Armenia, no. 26986/03, §§ 116-117, 15 November 2007, and Bukta and Others v. Hungary, no. 25691/04, § 37, ECHR 2007‑III).
